questions.q: In the PX4 formula (ActuatorEffectivenessRotors) the rotor torque is CT·(p × a) − CT·KM·a. What does the sign of CA_ROTORn_KM set?
options: The spin direction: plus for CCW, minus for CW
The motor position: plus ahead of the CG, minus behind it
The ESC type: plus for DShot, minus for PWM
The thrust axis: plus down, minus up in FRD
questions.explain: In module.yaml: "Use a positive value for a rotor with CCW rotation. Use a negative value for a rotor with CW rotation." The position is set by CA_ROTORn_PX/PY/PZ, the axis by CA_ROTORn_AX/AY/AZ.

questions.q: Dead cat: the front motors are 0.13 m ahead of the CG, the rear ones 0.15 m behind it. How will PX4 split the thrust in hover?
options: Equally, and the I term removes the moments from the CG offset
The front ones 15 % more than the rear (0.15/0.13)
The rear ones 15 % more than the front (0.15/0.13)
The front ones 30 % more, from the sum of both arms
questions.explain: For a zero pitching moment, T_front·0.13 = T_rear·0.15, hence T_front/T_rear = 1.154. The pseudo-inverse accounts for this right away; in the module's example u = 0.536 / 0.464.

questions.q: PX4, CA_METHOD = 1, MC_AIRMODE = 0. At 60 % thrust the pilot rolls hard while yawing, and the motors run out of range. What gives way first?
options: Roll: it is squeezed before yaw is added
Thrust: it is raised to make room
Yaw: it is added last and cut first
All axes shrink in the same proportion
questions.explain: mixAirmodeDisabled: thrust can only be reduced, then roll and pitch are squeezed, and yaw is added in mixYaw() and desaturated first (with the MINIMUM_YAW_MARGIN of 15 %). In the example: roll 100 %, yaw 15 %.

questions.q: How does MC_AIRMODE = 1 differ from 0 at nearly zero throttle?
options: No difference: airmode affects only the upper throttle stop
With 1 yaw is turned off to preserve roll
With 1 roll and pitch are squeezed and thrust is unchanged
With 1 thrust may be raised so the roll is executed
questions.explain: mixAirmodeRP desaturates along the thrust vector in both directions. In the example at 5 % throttle the roll went from 16 % to 100 %, and the thrust grew 6 times. That is why the parameter description asks you to keep airmode off while tuning.

questions.q: An X hexacopter with alternating PNPNPN rotation loses a motor, CA_FAILURE_MODE = 1. What does the pseudo-inverse do in hover?
questions.fragment:
PNPNPN, M0 lost, pinv hover u: [-0.    0.75  0.75 -0.    0.75  0.75]
healthy hover u: 0.50 each (W = 3, T/W = 2)
options: Sets M3 to 0, the other four carry W/4 each
Splits the weight equally over five motors, 0.6 each
Reverses M3 to restore yaw authority
Raises all five motors to 1.0, and the vehicle descends
questions.explain: To keep the moments at zero, the minimum-norm solution sets the opposite motor to 0 and the rest to 0.75 = 3/4. M3 sits at its lower bound, so some directions have no margin. Reversing the opposite motor exists only on the main branch (mode 2).

questions.q: The x500 motors (r = 0.246 m, KM = 0.05) are tilted 10° tangentially toward their reaction torques. What happens to yaw and thrust?
options: Yaw ×1.18, vertical thrust −10 %
Yaw ×1.84, vertical thrust −1.5 %
Yaw ×2.46, vertical thrust −0.4 %
Yaw is unchanged, a side force appears
questions.explain: Mz ∝ r·sinθ + KM·cosθ = 0.0427 + 0.0492 = 0.0920 against 0.05, that is ×1.84; Fz ∝ cos 10° = 0.985. The side forces of the CCW and CW pairs cancel each other.

questions.q: A dead cat matrix from PX4 is carried over to Betaflight with mmix. Which column must take the opposite sign?
options: Roll: in Betaflight the right motor gets +1.000
Yaw: in Betaflight a CW motor gets +1.000 instead of −1
Pitch: in mixerQuadX the rear motor gets +1
Throttle: in Betaflight it is negative
questions.explain: In mixerQuadX REAR_R has pitch = +1, while in PX4 and ArduPilot a rear motor is negative in pitch. Roll of a right motor is −1 everywhere, and yaw of a CW motor is −1 (Betaflight documentation: 1.0 = CCW, −1.0 = CW).

questions.q: ArduPilot, FRAME_CLASS = 15, the script calls MotorsMatrix:init(4) and then set_throttle_factor(0, 1.07). What happens?
options: The factor takes effect after a reboot
The script fails on the assert, the vehicle does not arm
The factor is silently applied to the first motor
The call returns false, the factor does not change
questions.explain: AP_MotorsMatrix::set_throttle_factor returns false if the matrix is already initialized (initialised_ok()) or the frame class is not Scripting Matrix. The throttle factor is set between add_motor_raw and init().
